messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1869994321 - hosted-api-us-east queue growth detected. p95 latency > 3s, p99 > 18s, queued requests > 18k and growing. Paging oncall @amelia. Summary: potential GPU pool exhaustion and autoscaler errors. Links: https://obs.example.com/fig/1869994321-dashboard

amelia (oncall): seeing the alert. pulling metrics now. which pool is hot?

sandeep (eng-sre): hosted-us-east-gpu-pool-3 is at 98% utilization. Provisioner show 12 pending nodes for 22 minutes. Autoscaler logs: 429 from cloud provider on instance create; backoff loop. Found many inflight requests to large-llama-13b-q4

amelia (oncall): any customer-facing errors yet? status page?

ops-bot: Notified customers with active incidents subscription. No public status page update yet. 27 support tickets tied to timeouts.

maria (infra): checking provisioner controller: logs show repeated api error: "QuotaExceeded: Insufficient GPUs in region" then fallback attempts 5x with exponential backoff. Also seeing image pull timeouts on new nodes (registry 502).

kevin (platform): that quota error is suspicious; infra ticket says we've got headroom in account but soft quota in placement group may be the real blocker. Opening cloud support case.

amelia (oncall): mitigate immediate customer impact: can we route non-critical requests to cpu-hosted fallback model or smaller quantized variant?

sandeep (eng-sre): yes. I can flip routing policy to allow graceful degradation: route model_alias large-llama-13b -> large-llama-13b-q4-lazy on hosted-instances but with lower concurrency. Will also enable prefix/KV caching to reduce new token work.

amelia (oncall): do it. post commands you run.

sandeep (eng-sre): running rollout: 
```bash
# reduce concurrency and enable fallback
redwoodctl routing set --env hosted-us-east --policy fallback:allow --match model=large-llama-13b --to large-llama-13b-q4-lazy --max-concurrency 8
redwoodctl cache enable --env hosted-us-east --scope prefix
```

sandeep (eng-sre): applied. verifying traffic shift...

maria (infra): while that's happening, I'm going to increase soft limits for provisioning and try alternateAZ. If cloud support fails, will spin up from a different placement pool. Running: 
```text
provisioner: request create 12 g4dn-type nodes -> alt-placement-group-2.
```

ops-bot: Reaction :thumbsup: from 3 people

kevin (platform): also temporarily enabling request-shedding for heavy routes to target 95th percentile SLO. This will return 429 for low-priority /batch endpoints.

amelia (oncall): note for postmortem: which customers impacted? tara, can you summarize customer tickets?

tara (customer-success): pulling tickets. Early glance: 14 paying customers reported increased 504s and timeouts; 3 reported degraded latency impacting production calls. Most on US-East. One large customer (acme.ai) reported spikes at 13:24 UTC leading to 30% request failures. I'm drafting a targeted notification.

sandeep (eng-sre): metrics update: queue dropped from 18k -> 7.4k after routing change. p95 down from 3.2s -> 1.1s. p99 still elevated at ~9.2s. Error rate decreased from 6.8% -> 2.1%.

amelia (oncall): good. Keep watch and timeline. If pending nodes don't become ready in 10m, escalate cloud case and consider cross-region spillover for critical traffic.

maria (infra): provisioner progress: 12 pending -> 6 provisioning -> 2 ready. image-pull failures persist on 2 nodes due to registry 502; retries in flight. Cloud support case created: INC-8421: placement capacity anomaly.

sandeep (eng-sre): additional mitigation: enable smaller model routing for chat endpoints for non-SLA customers and start token rate limiter to buy time. Command: 
```bash
redwoodctl rate-limit set --route /v1/chat --env hosted-us-east --limit 20rps --priority-signal low
```

ops-bot: posted: internal status update to #incidents-updates with link to this thread.

amelia (oncall): oncall handoff note: if this persists across shift, we need platform and infra on early morning to sort permanent fixes. For now, continue mitigation. Who's driving next 30m?

maria (infra): I'm on it. chasing cloud support + trying alt AZ fallback.

kevin (platform): I'll prepare a temporary model-shard to accept overflow traffic into dedicated pools in eu-west as spillover, but routing changes could add latency.

sandeep (eng-sre): quick log snippet from autoscaler: 
```text
2026-08-19T13:18:02Z autoscaler WARN: instance_create failed: 429 TooManyRequests, retrying in 45s
2026-08-19T13:19:03Z provisioner ERROR: node startup script: image pull failed, status 502
2026-08-19T13:19:55Z autoscaler INFO: scaled_to 32 gpus (target 44)
```

amelia (oncall): timeline note: alert fired 13:12 UTC, routing mitigation applied 13:26, queue started dropping by 13:31, initial cloud case created 13:34.

tara (customer-success): customer-facing message draft: 
"We're investigating increased latency and timeouts for Hosted API in US-East. We've applied temporary routing mitigations to reduce impact; some customers may experience degraded performance or 429s while we recover capacity. We'll follow up with ETA within 1 hour."

amelia (oncall): send that now to affected customers list and add status page update.

ops-bot: Sent status update to affected customers and posted to status.redwood.ai.

maria (infra): cloud support replied: "We see temporary AZ capacity constraints, retry using alternate placement group or different instance family." Attempting alternate instance family g5->a10 in alt group.

sandeep (eng-sre): monitoring metrics: p99 trending down slowly to 6.0s. Queues at 5.8k and falling. Error rate 1.4%.

amelia (oncall): good progress. moving to incident severity: SEV2 -> SEV3? I'd keep it SEV2 until p99 < 3s and queue < 1k.

kevin (platform): spun up spillover pool in eu-west and started routing critical customers with cross-region preference. Expect additional network latency ~80-120ms but avoids timeouts.

tara (customer-success): acme.ai confirmed lower failures after the routing change but seeing higher latencies; they're ok with mitigation for now. I'll keep them updated.

maria (infra): all 12 nodes now either ready or replaced. Provisioner reports node_count=44 gpus, autoscaler target satisfied. Cloud case awaiting follow-up.

sandeep (eng-sre): final metrics: queue 912, p95 0.98s, p99 2.8s, error rate 0.4%. Rolling back some temporary shedding and smaller-model routing to recover quality slowly.

amelia (oncall): rolling back: 
```bash
redwoodctl routing remove --env hosted-us-east --policy fallback:allow --match model=large-llama-13b
redwoodctl rate-limit delete --route /v1/chat --env hosted-us-east
```

sandeep (eng-sre): rollback applied. Monitoring closely.

ops-bot: Reaction :white_check_mark: from 5 people

amelia (oncall): incident update: capacity recovered, queue drained, p99 below 3s. Moving to monitoring state. Please add postmortem notes: root cause suspicion - AZ capacity + registry image-pull transient errors that amplified provisioning delay. Action items: (1) add alternate instance family fallback in autoscaler config, (2) pre-warm image cache in provisioner, (3) add soft quota alerts earlier, (4) update runbook for cross-region spillover, (5) review per-customer routing priorities.

maria (infra): filing infra-issue: INFRA-2107 (prewarm registry + placement fallback).

kevin (platform): adding autoscaler change request: PLAT-3343.

tara (customer-success): sending post-incident notes to affected customers with ETA on fixes.

amelia (oncall): handoff: I'm off in 45m. Sandeep will take ownership for the postmortem doc. If anything regresses, ping this thread.

sandeep (eng-sre): will own the postmortem. grabbing screenshots and graphs, will publish in #postmortems and link to incident ticket.

ops-bot: Incident 1869994321 moved to status: monitoring -> resolved_pending_postmortem.

amelia (oncall): thanks team. good work on quick mitigations and customer comms.
